title: BAGMAN MailboxMessage
description: A durable, provider-neutral PROJECTION of one email message discovered by a mailbox sweep (CD-6 Slice 4: first real mailbox adapter + sweep engine). This is NOT the evidence bytes (the raw MIME lives in the canonical `EvidenceItem`/object-store architecture, see `evidence_id` below) and NOT an accounting fact (no invoice/classification/AI field exists here — that is Slice 5). Canonical uniqueness is (mailbox_id, immutable_provider_message_id) — a message moving between folders (e.g. Inbox to Junk) never creates a second row; `observed_folder` simply reflects wherever the message was last seen.

mailbox_message_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this message projection row.

mailbox_id.description: The `MailboxSource` this message was swept from.

provider_kind.description: Deliberately open (mirrors `MailboxSource.provider_kind`'s own contract-layer doctrine) — the provider family this message was observed through, e.g. `MICROSOFT_GRAPH`.

immutable_provider_message_id.description: The provider's own IMMUTABLE, case-sensitive message identifier (for Microsoft Graph: the `Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId"` id). Canonical uniqueness for this contract is (mailbox_id, immutable_provider_message_id) — enforced at the repository/database layer, not by this schema alone.

internet_message_id.description: The RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header value, if present. METADATA ONLY — never the idempotency key (a provider may legitimately reuse/omit this across distinct provider messages); see `immutable_provider_message_id` above for the real identity key.

observed_folder.description: CD-6 architect amendment (recursive folder discovery). The provider's own real, immutable folder identifier (e.g. Microsoft Graph's own resolved folder id) this message was most recently observed in — deliberately OPEN (no longer a closed Inbox/Junk enum): the monitored set now includes Inbox, Junk Email, Deleted Items, and every custom/nested/hidden folder the mailbox's own folder discovery surfaces (Sent Items/Drafts/Outbox are excluded from monitoring entirely and never appear here). This is the CANONICAL, gate-relevant value — never a display name; see `observed_folder_display_name` for the human-readable counterpart.

observed_folder_display_name.description: CD-6 architect amendment (recursive folder discovery). The human-readable label for `observed_folder`'s own real folder id, for GUI/operator display ONLY — never used for identity, gating, or cursor lookup. `null` for a row created before this amendment, or when a caller genuinely has no display name to report.

subject.description: Untrusted provider-supplied string — never rendered as HTML, never treated as an instruction of any kind.

sender_address.description: Untrusted provider-supplied sender email address string.

sender_display_name.description: Untrusted provider-supplied sender display name string.

sender_domain.description: CD-6 architect amendment (two-stage mail processing). The domain portion of `sender_address`, lowercased — stored explicitly (rather than only derived on demand) because it is the actual gate key `services.mailbox.domain_rule.MailboxDomainRuleRepository.find_for_sender` matches against. `null` only when `sender_address` itself is absent/unparseable.

received_at.description: The provider's own `receivedDateTime` for this message.

has_attachments.description: Provider-reported attachment flag. The whole message (headers, body, attachments) is stored as one immutable `.eml` evidence artifact once ingested (see `evidence_id`) — this flag and `attachment_metadata` below exist purely for the Stage-A discovery gate; this slice never extracts/parses individual attachment CONTENT.

attachment_metadata.description: CD-6 architect amendment (Stage A discovery — 'attachment metadata sufficient for discovery'). Bounded, discovery-only per-attachment metadata (filename/content type/size) — NEVER attachment bytes/content. Empty when `has_attachments` is `false`, or when the provider attachment listing itself could not be retrieved (a best-effort discovery signal, never a blocking failure).

auth_signals.description: CD-6 architect amendment (§7 — authentication/spoofing). Provider-supplied authentication-domain signals (SPF/DKIM/DMARC-alignment-style), captured SEPARATELY from the visible `sender_address`/`sender_domain` — never used by this slice to silently trust or distrust a message, only preserved honestly for a later stage. Each key is one of `spf`/`dkim`/`dmarc`; each value is whatever short verdict token the provider actually supplied (e.g. `"pass"`/`"fail"`/`"softfail"`/`"none"`), or `null` when the provider supplied nothing parseable for that mechanism — this slice never invents a verdict Graph did not actually return.

evidence_id.description: The canonical `EvidenceItem` holding this message's immutable raw `.eml` bytes, once ingestion has succeeded. `null` while `ingestion_status` is not yet a terminal success (e.g. `QUARANTINED`/`FAILED` — a quarantined message's bytes live under the evidence architecture's own quarantine path, referenced by `EvidenceItem`/provenance records, not by this field).

ingestion_status.description: Outcome of this message's own Stage-A/Stage-B processing attempt (CD-6 architect amendment — two-stage mail processing; CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on WO added `SECURITY_REVIEW`). `INGESTED` — a real `EvidenceItem` exists (`evidence_id` is set); only reachable via a `MUST_READ` `MailboxDomainRule` whose own per-message authentication check passed. `QUARANTINED` — the content-safety scanner flagged it; retained via the governed quarantine path, never parsed, never silently discarded. `FAILED` — an oversized message or another explicit terminal ingestion fault. `VANISHED` — the message existed in a delta page but had disappeared by the time its MIME content was fetched (a real, deterministic, recorded outcome — never a fabricated evidence row). `CHECKED_NOT_CANDIDATE` — this message was observed and its sender gate was evaluated (a `BLACKLIST`/`GRAYLIST` rule matched, or no rule matched and `services.mailbox.discovery_signals` found no credible accounting-document signal) — seen, checked, deliberately never fetched/stored beyond this discovery projection (architect §9's data-volume doctrine). `SECURITY_REVIEW` — a `MUST_READ`-policy message whose own SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication signals failed a bounded, deterministic check; a genuine candidate that failed a security check, never MIME-fetched/evidence-created via the normal trusted path, and never counted toward the same 'is this domain relevant' question a `MAILBOX_DOMAIN_REVIEW` item asks — see `services/mailbox/sweep.py`'s own module docstring.

first_seen_at.description: UTC timestamp this message was FIRST discovered by any sweep.

last_seen_at.description: UTC timestamp this message was MOST RECENTLY observed by a sweep (e.g. re-seen after moving folders, or a safe idempotent replay).

metadata.description: Free-form, non-secret context (e.g. the sweep_run_id that first discovered this message). Never raw MIME/body content — see this contract's own top-level description.

discovery_candidate.description: Second CD-6 architect amendment (persisted discovery decision). `true` only when `services.mailbox.discovery_signals.evaluate_discovery_candidate` actually ran for this message AND judged it a credible financial-document candidate. `false` when the heuristic ran and judged it NOT credible. `null` when the heuristic never ran at all — the honest state for an `IGNORED`-domain message (the domain gate short-circuits before Stage-A candidate evaluation ever executes) and for any `ALLOWED`-domain message (never sits in a discovery-only state at all), or for a row created before this amendment.

discovery_reason.description: Second CD-6 architect amendment (persisted discovery decision). The bounded, non-AI heuristic's own honest explanation of what it matched (e.g. "subject contains keyword 'invoice'") — set ONLY when `discovery_candidate` is `true`. `null` for the `discovery_candidate == false` case (no reason is required there) and for the `discovery_candidate == null` case (heuristic never ran).

discovery_checked_at.description: Second CD-6 architect amendment (persisted discovery decision). UTC timestamp Stage-A/B discovery processing actually happened for this message — set whenever discovery-only handling ran (both the `IGNORED`-domain branch AND the UNKNOWN-domain branch), regardless of `discovery_candidate`. `null` for any message that never went through discovery-only handling at all (an `ALLOWED`-domain message, or a row created before this amendment).
